pme.answer: Yes, that is often where it pays back fastest. The audit finds them, puts a number on that time and checks that an automation costs less than what it saves.

whatIs.question: Is GEO just SEO for ChatGPT?
whatIs.answer: Partly. GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization: the work that makes a site readable and citable by AI engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google's AI Overviews. SEO aims for a rank in a list of links. GEO aims for a place among the few sources an AI engine cites in its answer. The two overlap a lot.

guarantee.question: Can you guarantee ChatGPT will cite me?
guarantee.answer: No, and nobody can honestly promise that. AI engines change their answers from one week to the next and do not publish their rules. What we commit to is the method: a baseline, documented fixes on your pages, and the same measurement at day 30 on the same questions. You see what moved, with the numbers to back it.

vsSeo.question: Should I stop doing classic SEO?
vsSeo.answer: No. AI engines rely largely on the same signals as Google: fast, well-structured pages with clear answers and verifiable facts. Good SEO is still the base. GEO adds direct answers at the top of the page, structured data, an llms.txt file and tracking of what AI engines say about you, question by question.

problems.title: Repetitive work
problems.body: AI automation for an accounting or law firm takes over reading and data entry, and a staff member approves every sensitive step. In a firm of 10 to 50 people, part of the week goes into sorting the shared inbox, re-keying invoices and statements, chasing missing documents and rebuilding the same dashboard every month. These tasks always follow the same steps.

items.inbox: A shared inbox sorted by hand every morning
items.docs: Invoices, statements and receipts re-keyed into the software
items.chase: Reminders for missing documents written one by one
items.report: The same monthly report rebuilt in a spreadsheet

secret.question: Is professional secrecy compatible with an AI tool?
secret.answer: Yes, if the data is processed within a framework you control. Accounts stay in your name, we can choose an EU-hosted model provider, mask names and amounts before sending, or keep some steps free of AI. We set that framework with you during the audit. Your profession's rules remain the reference.

software.question: Does it work with our accounting software?
software.answer: Often, but not always directly. When the software has an API or a file import, the workflow drops the entries there for approval. Otherwise it prepares a file ready to import by hand. We check your software during the audit, and tell you what is possible before we price the workflow.

staff.question: Does our staff need training?
staff.answer: A little. They keep their usual tools and approve what the workflow prepares for them. We plan an onboarding session at delivery and short documentation written for them. If a staff member needs to change a step themselves, we show them how to do it in your automation tool.

roi.question: How do we know whether AI is worth the cost?
roi.answer: By comparing two numbers: the time the task takes today and the price of the automation. If someone spends five hours a week keying in invoices, the automation is measured against those hours. The AI audit does that calculation task by task. Our prices are set in writing before we start, so the cost doesn't move along the way.

rgpd.question: Can an AI project comply with GDPR?
rgpd.answer: Yes, if it is designed to. Before writing code, we list the personal data the automation handles, keep only what it needs, and set a retention period. Accounts stay in your name. If your data is sensitive, we choose EU hosting or mask some fields before they are sent to the model.

aiAct.question: Does the AI Act apply to our project?
aiAct.answer: Rarely in a heavy way for an SME. Sorting email, extracting invoices or answering product questions are not among the high-risk uses. CV screening or assessing the creditworthiness of individuals are. An assistant that talks to your customers must say it is an AI, and the team using an AI tool must understand its limits. We plan for both. For legal advice, ask your lawyer.

expertise.question: We have no AI skills at all. Is that a problem?
expertise.answer: No, that is the case for most SMEs. We handle the technical side, your team keeps its usual tools and approves what the AI prepares. Every delivery includes onboarding and written documentation, and what we build stays with you: the code in your repository, the n8n or Make automations in your accounts. Nobody needs to know how to write a prompt.

useful.question: How do we know whether AI can help our business?
useful.answer: Think of a task that comes back every week: reading email, re-keying documents, chasing clients. If it follows roughly the same steps each time, it can probably be partly automated. Book a 30-minute call: we pick one with you and tell you honestly whether it's worth it.

continuity.question: What happens if Klyx is no longer available?
continuity.answer: Your project keeps running. The code is in your repository from day one, the n8n or Make automations sit in your accounts with their export, the tools are in your name, and every project ends with a written handover. Any developer can take over from that documentation, without depending on us.
